risks.description: Macro-fiscal constraints, declining government revenues, and high national debt burdens in participating countries could reduce counterpart allocations and jeopardize the long-term financial sustainability of health security investments.
risks.mitigation: Technical assistance will be provided to help ministries of finance and health integrate health security into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, track budgets, and explore public-private partnerships.
risks.evidence: declining oil revenues and structural economic challenges... high debt burden limits public investment in health

risks.description: Ongoing armed conflict, active insurgency, and socio-political violence in FCV regions (such as Lake Chad Basin, CAR, and NW/SW Cameroon) could restrict field access, threaten personnel safety, and interrupt health activities.
risks.mitigation: Prepare and implement country-specific Security Risk Assessments (SRAs) and Security Management Plans (SMPs), alongside flexible implementation modalities in FCV zones.
risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence, leading to large population displacements.

risks.description: Increased laboratory diagnostic activities and civil works could generate hazardous healthcare, chemical, biological, and construction waste, posing serious environmental and community health hazards if mismanaged.
risks.mitigation: Implement updated National Healthcare Waste Management Plans, site-specific ESMPs, and biosafety guidelines across all project-supported laboratory and health facilities.
risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

risks.description: Procurement bottlenecks, limited local vendor competition in FCV environments, and complex multi-country procurement could lead to significant project implementation delays.
risks.mitigation: Deploy hands-on procurement coaching, utilize STEP for tracking, conduct early market engagement, and explore joint regional bulk procurement options where appropriate.
risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

risks.description: Delays in recruiting and onboarding critical PIU technical, financial, M&E, and environmental/social specialists could hamper project startup and operational execution.
risks.mitigation: Enforce legal covenants requiring specialist recruitment within 1-3 months of effectiveness and leverage existing experienced PIU structures where available.
risks.evidence: The Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, appoint, assign, or recruit

risks.description: Inconsistent cross-border protocols, regulatory barriers, and inter-institutional coordination frictions among CEMAC, WAHO, and national authorities could slow real-time data sharing and rapid emergency response.
risks.mitigation: Establish formal legal MoUs and utilize the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC) facilitated by CEMAC and WAHO to harmonize data-sharing standards and cross-border SOPs.
risks.evidence: disease outbreaks often cross borders, making coordinated cross-border collaboration essential, as fragmented efforts hinder effective response.

risks.description: Expanded frontline health deployments, community outreach, and labor influx for infrastructure works create substantial risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
risks.mitigation: Enforce worker codes of conduct, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, establish survivor-centered Grievance Redress Mechanisms, and execute country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans.
risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... increased presence of new health workforce... may create concerns

risks.description: Persistent baseline gaps in laboratory diagnostic infrastructure, quality management, and genomic sequencing capacity could impede timely detection and characterization of dangerous pathogens.
risks.mitigation: Invest in SLIPTA quality accreditation, establish regional reference laboratory networks, upgrade biosafety/biosecurity systems, and operationalize LIMS and genomic sequencing capabilities.
risks.evidence: the region commonly faces significant gaps in laboratory diagnostic capabilities, disease surveillance and information systems

risks.description: Substantial financial management residual risks, including weak internal controls and decentralized activities in remote areas, could lead to financial non-compliance or questionable expenditures.
risks.mitigation: Customize accounting software within three months of effectiveness, conduct regular internal audit risk reviews, deploy standardized procedure manuals, and perform independent external audits.
risks.evidence: The overall FM residual risk rating is assessed as Substantial... activities at risk to generate questionable expenditures in remote areas

risks.description: Severe climate shocks such as frequent flooding, extreme heatwaves, and droughts could destroy healthcare infrastructure and trigger widespread outbreaks of climate-sensitive vector-borne and waterborne diseases.
risks.mitigation: Integrate climate adaptation and resilient green infrastructure criteria into health facility refurbishments and link public health surveillance to climate early-warning systems.
risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 percent of natural disasters... mostly constituted of floods, epidemics, and droughts.

risks.description: Severe public health emergencies risk overstretching national health systems, causing resources to be diverted away from routine primary care and interrupting essential maternal and child health services.
risks.mitigation: Develop and adopt national service continuity plans, strengthen primary healthcare contingency capacity, and monitor routine service delivery indicators during crises.
risks.evidence: health emergencies... disrupt services like maternal and child health, immunization, and chronic disease management weakening population health

risks.description: Inadequate community engagement and communication barriers could result in the exclusion of vulnerable groups, such as IDPs, refugees, rural women, and indigenous communities, from emergency services.
risks.mitigation: Implement inclusive Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), deploy targeted Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) strategies, and monitor functional Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to... the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

risks.description: Gender bias and societal constraints limiting female participation in advanced technical training (FETP/FELTP/ISAVET) could perpetuate workforce gender gaps and reduce community-level response efficacy.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate explicit gender targets, offer flexible training formats, and proactively recruit female health and veterinary workers into field epidemiology programs.
risks.evidence: women remain underrepresented in formal epidemiological training and decision-making... underrepresented in key technical roles

risks.description: Delays in procuring and customizing dedicated multi-project accounting software across national PIUs could delay financial reporting and jeopardize timely grant/credit disbursements.
risks.mitigation: Include software customization as a key legal covenant with strict 3-month post-effectiveness deadlines and provide dedicated FM technical assistance during rollout.
risks.evidence: customize the existing accounting software to include the bookkeeping for the Project... no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date

risks.description: Weak supply chain infrastructure and logistics bottlenecks in remote and conflict-affected zones could lead to critical stockouts of essential diagnostic kits, personal protective equipment, and vaccines.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen emergency supply chains, establish national and regional stockpiles, deploy digital logistics tracking systems, and utilize solar-powered cold chains.
risks.evidence: supply chain infrastructure and management... frequent drug stock out... difficulties in deploying timely responses
